item.title: Sqwod Daily · Thursday, 26 November 2026
item.description: Nuffield Health is rolling out Hyrox training across 70 UK clubs by 2028, included in standard memberships at no extra cost to members.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, 26 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Thursday, 26 November 2026 · Weekday
Nuffield Health brings Hyrox to 70 UK clubs, milon launches velocity-based strength system & New Balance signs lifetime deal with Ohtani
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Nuffield Health is rolling out Hyrox training across 70 UK clubs by 2028, included in standard memberships at no extra cost to members.
Sqwod
 
Connect the dots
Nuffield Health absorbs Hyrox into standard membership at 70 clubs
Nuffield Health, a nonprofit healthcare and fitness operator, has begun rolling out official Hyrox training programs across its UK health clubs. More than 35 locations are expected to offer the programming by January 2027, with 70 clubs targeted by 2028. The rollout includes classes, specialist coaching and in-club race simulations, all covered by standard membership fees. Nuffield Health has invested in dedicated training spaces, specialised equipment and instructor training at participating clubs to support the program.
For studio and gym operators watching competitive fitness formats, the key signal here is pricing. A large membership network is absorbing Hyrox, classes, coaching and all, at no additional charge to members. If this becomes the norm among major operators, it sets a price expectation that makes it harder for independent studios to charge a premium for Hyrox-specific programming. Operators building Hyrox offerings should consider how they will differentiate on quality, community or coaching depth rather than access alone.
 
The rundown
01
Nuffield Health to bring Hyrox training to 70 UK clubs by 2028
Nuffield Health, a nonprofit healthcare and fitness operator, has begun rolling out official Hyrox training programs across its UK health clubs, with more than 35 locations expected to offer the programming by January 2027 and 70 clubs targeted by 2028. Classes, specialist coaching and in-club race simulations are included in standard memberships at no extra cost, backed by investment in dedicated training spaces, equipment and instructor training. Operators watching competitive fitness formats should note that a large membership network is absorbing Hyrox at no additional charge to members, which sets a price expectation in that segment.
Source: Athletech News →
02
milon launches Velocity Based Training system for strength equipment
Equipment manufacturer milon has introduced milon Velocity Based Training, a strength training system that measures the speed of every repetition to assess neuromuscular output, fatigue and whether the intended training stimulus was reached. The system automatically detects performance drops and adjusts load based on objective data rather than estimates. For studio operators, the product positions velocity-based load management, already common in elite sport, as a commercial gym offering.
Source: body LIFE →
03
New Balance signs lifetime deal with Shohei Ohtani, renames innovation lab after him
New Balance has signed a lifetime partnership with four-time baseball MVP Shohei Ohtani, who joined the brand in 2023 and has worked with its designers and sports scientists on performance footwear and apparel. The company also renamed its innovation facility the Shohei Ohtani Sports Research Lab, as New Balance reported $9.2 billion in 2025 sales and continued expanding in Japan, where Ohtani plays a central role in its global strategy. For brands and investors in the performance category, the deal signals that lifetime athlete partnerships tied directly to product development, not just endorsement, are becoming a tool for long-term market positioning.
Source: Fitt Insider →

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Wednesday, 25 November 2026
item.description: Club Pilates has debuted a redesigned studio concept at a California location, while Midtown Athletic Club added a strength programme and a Newcastle gym raised £10,159 for Alzheimer's Research UK.
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday, 25 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Wednesday, 25 November 2026 · Weekday
Club Pilates refreshes studio design ahead of 20th anniversary, Midtown launches FORGE strength programme & £10k raised for dementia research
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Club Pilates has debuted a redesigned studio concept at a California location, while Midtown Athletic Club added a strength programme and a Newcastle gym raised £10,159 for Alzheimer's Research UK.
Sqwod
 
Connect the dots
Club Pilates rolls out new studio design as Pilates competition grows
Club Pilates debuted a redesigned studio concept at its Foothill Ranch, California location in July 2026. The refresh covers lighting, equipment, finishes, lobby and retail areas. All new locations will open with the design as standard. Existing franchisees can choose to upgrade, though the upgrade is optional rather than required. The brand approaches its 20th anniversary in 2027 as newer Pilates concepts compete for the same members.
For studio operators considering a refit, the Club Pilates rollout sets a visible benchmark for what a refreshed Pilates environment now looks like. The optional upgrade model means franchisees will be watching take-up rates across the network before committing their own capital. Independent Pilates studio owners face the same question: whether updated finishes and retail presentation are enough to hold members as the category becomes more crowded.
 
The rundown
01
Club Pilates rolls out refreshed studio design ahead of 20th anniversary
Club Pilates debuted a redesigned studio concept at its Foothill Ranch, California location in July, featuring updated lighting, equipment, finishes, and redesigned lobby and retail areas. New locations will open with the design by default, and existing franchisees can choose to upgrade. With competition in the Pilates segment intensifying and newer concepts competing for the same members, operators considering a refit will be watching whether the optional upgrade programme gains traction across the franchise network.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Midtown Athletic Club launches FORGE strength training at two Chicago-area clubs
Midtown Athletic Club launched FORGE, a strength training programme using XFormer spring-resistance equipment, at its Bannockburn and Palatine locations in Chicago's suburbs. The programme uses spring resistance, a moving carriage and controlled movements to create continuous muscular engagement with low joint impact. FORGE is included in the standard Midtown membership rather than sold as a separate add-on, a model that positions full-service clubs as direct competitors to boutique strength studios.
Source: Club Solutions →
03
£10,159 raised for Alzheimer's Research UK in Newcastle gym's 10-hour challenge
Patrick (PD) Savage, owner of Savage WPL gym in Newcastle, County Down, ran a 10-hour community fitness event called '1 Million Metres for Dementia' on 24 October 2026, raising £10,159 for Alzheimer's Research UK, or £11,722 when Gift Aid tax relief is included. Participants hit one million metres by lunchtime and completed over two million metres by 5pm; Savage presented a cheque to Alzheimer's Research UK representative Hazel Stirling. The event shows how gym operators can structure a large-scale community fundraiser around a measurable fitness goal to drive participation and significant charitable income.
Source: Down News →
04
ELV Active, Beyond Yoga and SPIbelt launch Black Friday discounts
Several activewear brands launched Black Friday promotions, with ELV Active offering up to 50% off its sets, Beyond Yoga cutting 30% off all products and up to 75% off sale styles, and SPIbelt starting its deal from 27 November. Alo Yoga, Aviator Nation, Vuori and Adidas are also named among brands running offers this season, according to Athletech News. For studio operators buying kit in bulk or advising clients on gear, the Beyond Yoga sitewide discount and the deep ELV Active cut are the most clearly defined savings available now.
Source: Athletech News →
05
Listening bars and tea houses emerge as wellness third places beyond gyms
Listening bars, tea houses, book clubs, chess clubs, and creative spaces are gaining attention as wellness alternatives that prioritise community over performance tracking or health optimisation, according to Fitt Insider. These concepts centre on the idea of a third place, a space beyond home and work, where people connect and spend time together offline. For wellness operators, the signal is that people may return more reliably to a space built around community than to one built around a service or product alone.
Source: Fitt Insider →
 
Stat
£11,722
Total raised for Alzheimer's Research UK including Gift Aid by Savage WPL gym's 10-hour challenge on 24 October 2026
The figure shows that a single community fitness event structured around a measurable goal, one million metres of collective movement, can generate meaningful charitable income for a small gym operator.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Tuesday, 24 November 2026
item.description: Most NHS local health boards in England have withdrawn GP prescribing payments for Mounjaro, potentially reducing patient flow to weight-management programmes tied to primary care referrals.
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday, 24 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Tuesday, 24 November 2026 · Weekday
NHS GP Mounjaro access tightens, Ohana sells 7 Florida Planet Fitness clubs & Therme reveals £500m Manchester resort
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Most NHS local health boards in England have withdrawn GP prescribing payments for Mounjaro, potentially reducing patient flow to weight-management programmes tied to primary care referrals.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Valuation
Therme Manchester

⇄  Acquired
Ohana Growth Partners

Connect the dots
NHS pulls GP payments for Mounjaro: what it means for weight-management programmes
A report by Pulse found that most local health boards in England have withdrawn dedicated payments for GPs to prescribe and monitor Mounjaro, a weight-loss drug available on the NHS. Without those payments, GPs have less financial incentive to prescribe the drug, meaning patients who qualify may struggle to access it through primary care.
For operators running weight-management or GP-referral programmes that depend on Mounjaro prescriptions, the change could reduce the number of patients reaching their facilities through that route. If your programme is built around GP-referred members on Mounjaro, now is a good time to review how your referral pipeline works and whether it depends on a single access point.
 
The rundown
01
Most NHS local health boards drop Mounjaro prescribing payments, Pulse reports
A report by Pulse found that most local health boards in England have withdrawn dedicated payments for GPs to prescribe and monitor Mounjaro, a weight-loss drug available on the NHS. Patients in England who qualify for the drug through the NHS could struggle to get it prescribed by their GP as a result. Fitness operators running weight-management or GP-referral programmes tied to Mounjaro prescriptions may see patient numbers affected if access through primary care tightens.
Source: Health Club Management →
02
Superpower cuts membership to $179 for Black Friday
Biomarker testing service Superpower, founded in 2023, is selling its membership at $179 for Black Friday, down from $199. The membership covers a blood draw across a network of more than 3,000 labs nationwide including Quest Diagnostics, a full report with 17 health scores, a personalized action plan and unlimited access to an AI-powered concierge; it is HSA- and FSA-eligible but not covered by insurance. For fitness operators and coaches watching the health data space, a blood-testing service that tests more than 100 biomarkers and flags early signs of over 1,000 conditions is now within reach of a wider consumer price point.
Source: Athletech News →
03
Ohana Growth Partners sells 7 Florida Planet Fitness clubs to Gulf Coast Fitness Management
Ohana Growth Partners, one of the largest Planet Fitness franchisees, sold its seven Florida clubs, totalling nearly 134,000 square feet, to Gulf Coast Fitness Management. Gulf Coast Fitness Management also holds development rights for 20 Planet Fitness clubs along Florida's west coast from St. Petersburg to Naples, plus rights for three new clubs in Broward and Palm Beach County. The deal signals active consolidation and expansion among Planet Fitness franchisees on Florida's Gulf Coast.
Source: Club Solutions →
04
166,000 non-member visits recorded in 'United let's move.' campaign
The 'United let's move.' fitness campaign, reported by DSSV, drew more than 166,000 training visits from non-members during the European Week of Sport, which ran from 23 to 30 September 2026. A total of 1,950 fitness and health facilities in Germany and Austria, plus around 7,500 additional partner studios through aggregators, took part, and non-member visits rose 41.1 percent year on year, with over 3.1 million total training visits recorded across participating studios. For operators, the figures show that open-door campaign weeks can convert significant numbers of non-members into first-time visitors.
Source: DSSV →
05
Athletech News publishes 2026 holiday gift guide for fitness and wellness
Athletech News published a gift guide covering fitness and wellness products for men, including recovery gadgets, athletic apparel, open-ear headphones and red light caps. The guide highlights Superpower, a blood testing service that measures over 100 biomarkers from a single blood draw, covering markers such as testosterone, ApoB, inflammation markers, ferritin and vitamin D. The outlet said it will update its shopping guides regularly through the holiday season.
Source: Athletech News →
06
Therme reveals updated designs for £500m Manchester wellness resort
Therme Manchester has shared revised plans for its £500m (US$656m) wellness resort at a 28-acre TraffordCity site, as construction moves forward. Therme Group vice-president of global impact Ramona Chiriac also set out the company's goal to make wellbeing accessible at scale through large destination venues. For operators, the project signals growing investor appetite for large-format wellness facilities positioned as public infrastructure rather than premium-only products.
Source: Health Club Management →
 
Policy watch
NHS local health boards pull GP prescribing payments for Mounjaro
Most local health boards in England have withdrawn dedicated payments for GPs to prescribe and monitor Mounjaro, the weight-loss drug available on the NHS. Studios and coaches running weight-management or GP-referral programmes should monitor whether this reduces the number of patients being directed into their services through primary care.

Non-member visits rose 41.1 percent year on year across 1,950 fitness and health facilities in Germany and Austria plus around 7,500 partner studios through aggregators, showing that structured open-door campaign weeks can bring significant numbers of first-time visitors through the door.

DAILY
Monday, 23 November 2026 · Weekday
Hone Health raises $228M in longevity funding, Zing Coach AI platform for gym operators & TOUCH:BAY opens free ad space to health non-profits
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Hone Health closed $228M in new funding, while Zing Coach offers AI-personalised coaching integrations for gym operators and TOUCH:BAY opens its studio screens to health non-profits.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
Hone Health

Connect the dots
Zing Coach brings AI personalised coaching to gym operators
Zing Coach Inc. built an AI fitness coaching platform that creates training plans based on a member's goals, available equipment, training history and schedule, then adjusts those plans using activity data and member feedback. Gym and studio partners can deploy it as a branded experience inside the Zing app, embed it through a mobile software development kit (a toolkit that lets developers add features to an existing app), or pursue a full white-label app. Independent reporting confirms the platform is already live with gym operators.
For studio and gym operators evaluating digital coaching tools, Zing Coach offers three integration paths at different levels of brand control. Because the platform uses ongoing member feedback to adjust plans, it can serve members with varying experience levels without manual reprogramming by coaches. Operators should confirm partner pricing and commercial terms directly with Zing Coach before committing.
 
The rundown
01
Hone Health raises $228M in longevity funding
Hone Health secured $228 million in new funding, according to Axios.
Source: Axios →
02
Zing Coach offers AI workout platform with branded app options for gym operators
Zing Coach Inc. has built an AI fitness coaching platform that personalises training plans based on goals, equipment, training history and schedules, then adjusts those plans using activity data and member feedback. Gym and studio partners can deploy it as a branded experience inside the Zing app, embed it via a mobile software development kit, or pursue a white-label app. Independent reporting confirms the platform has been deployed with gym operators, making it a live option for fitness businesses evaluating personalised digital coaching within a branded member experience.
Source: Quasa.io →
03
TOUCH:BAY opens its gym display network to non-profit health campaigns
TOUCH:BAY, a digital display network that runs screens inside fitness studios, has opened applications for non-profit organisations, associations and initiatives focused on health and quality of life to run their campaigns at no cost. Eligible campaigns include projects covering prevention, mental health, physical activity, inclusion, self-help and support for people with illness; applications are open now and selection will be based on how well each campaign fits the network's themes. Studio operators whose screens carry this network can offer wall space to community health causes without any action on their part, which may strengthen ties with local organisations.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
04
Zygo Z2 underwater headphones offered at 20% off for Black Friday
Zygo is offering its Z2 Waterproof Headphones at 20% off for Black Friday. The Z2 uses bone conduction technology to stream audio from a phone via a charging case that also acts as a transmitter, and the headphones are eligible for health savings and flexible spending accounts. Swim coaches and aquatic facility operators looking for audio tools for their clients have a time-limited price point to consider.
Source: Athletech News →

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Sunday, 22 November 2026
item.description: Chris Hemsworth's KINSYN longevity platform is live, and Nike Strength has added a $2,199 connected resistance trainer to its lineup.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday, 22 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Sunday, 22 November 2026 · Weekday
KINSYN longevity platform launches with Hemsworth & Nike Strength adds $2,199 Voltra I smart trainer
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Chris Hemsworth's KINSYN longevity platform is live, and Nike Strength has added a $2,199 connected resistance trainer to its lineup.
Sqwod
 
Connect the dots
KINSYN launches a data-driven longevity platform with Hemsworth
Chris Hemsworth co-founded and launched KINSYN, a health platform that pulls together bloodwork, wearable data, health history, and personal goals to build individualised wellness plans. The platform sells supplements, performance support, and physician-guided treatments covering weight management, skin health, and hair health. Its most detailed entry point is a comprehensive biomarker panel that tests more than 50 markers across metabolic, cardiovascular, thyroid, hormone, inflammation, stress, iron, and nutrient categories, with testing available at a lab or at home through a licensed phlebotomist.
For studio and gym operators offering nutrition or recovery services, KINSYN represents a well-funded, celebrity-backed model competing directly for the same client spending. Studios that do not already provide some form of data-driven health programming may find clients drawn toward platforms like this for guidance they once sought from their coach.
 
The rundown
01
Chris Hemsworth launches KINSYN, a personalized longevity platform
Actor and co-founder Chris Hemsworth launched KINSYN, a health platform that combines bloodwork, wearable data, health history, and individual goals to build personalized wellness plans. The platform offers supplements, performance support, and physician-guided treatments for weight management, skin, and hair health, with its most detailed entry point being a comprehensive biomarker panel testing more than 50 markers across metabolic, cardiovascular, thyroid, hormone, inflammation, stress, iron, and nutrient categories, administered at a lab or at home by a licensed phlebotomist. The launch signals growing consumer appetite for data-driven, individualized health programs that go beyond general fitness, which studios and coaches offering nutrition or recovery services may want to monitor as a competing model for client spend.
Source: Wellworthy →
02
Nike Strength adds $2,199 Voltra I smart resistance trainer to its lineup
Dimension 6 Fitness, the Nike licensee behind Nike Strength and Jordan Strength equipment, has partnered with fitness technology company Beyond Power to sell Beyond Power's Voltra I portable cable trainer on NikeStrength.com, priced at $2,199. The Voltra I uses a motor to generate up to 230 pounds of electronic resistance, adjustable in one-pound increments, in a device weighing 12.8 pounds. The move comes as Nike has stated plans for performance sports to generate $4 billion in additional annual revenue by fiscal 2031, signalling that connected strength equipment is becoming part of major brand strategies that studio and gym operators will need to account for.
Source: Athletech News →

Nike's stated target signals that connected strength equipment is becoming a core part of major brand strategies, which operators should factor into their equipment purchasing and partnership decisions.

Workout Anytime signs 15-club Southeast deal, FitX opens 115th gym & FitNation München draws 100 operators
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Workout Anytime nearly triples a franchisee's portfolio with a 15-club agreement, while FitX invested €2.5m in its newest Düsseldorf location and 100 operators met in Munich.
Sqwod

The rundown
01
FitNation München draws ~100 studio operators on 25 November
Around 100 gym and studio operators gathered at the NH München Ost Conference Center on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 for FitNation München, a half-day event organised by and for the fitness industry. Sessions covered revenue growth from existing members, payment failure and chargeback reduction under SEPA direct debit (the dominant payment method in Germany, Austria and Switzerland), and growth levers including artificial intelligence, sales automation and medical weight loss. The former IHRSA Director of Europe, now Director of International Business Development at FIT-C, presented on improving revenue mix without growing membership.
Source: body LIFE →
02
FitX opens 115th gym in Düsseldorf with €2.5m investment
FitX opened its fifth Düsseldorf location, in the Friedrichstadt district at Herzogstraße 15, on 21 November 2026, investing around 2.5 million euros in a 2,200-square-metre, two-floor facility with seven training zones including a gymnastics area of more than 180 square metres and a 300-square-metre group exercise studio. Regular live classes, 37 per week, begin on 21 December 2026, with a taster class schedule starting 7 December. The scale of investment and the density of group class programming signal that large low-cost operators are competing hard on facility quality and timetable breadth, not just on price.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
03
Munich Ravens used EGYM kit to test players for 2027 season
The Munich Ravens, a American football club, held a tryout day at the Sportschule Oberhaching sports facility on 17 November 2026, presented by EGYM. The EGYM Fitness Hub measured body composition and squat flexibility, while EGYM Smart Strength machines recorded maximum strength after sprint and jump tests run by the coaching team. Existing squad members were assessed in the morning and prospective new players completed the same diagnostic setup in the afternoon, with results feeding directly into roster decisions for the 2027 season.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
04
Workout Anytime signs 15-club deal to grow Southeast portfolio to 23 locations
Workout Anytime signed a 15-club development agreement with Tri South Fitness, an investment group led by franchisee Steven Elliott, on 19 November 2026, expanding Elliott's portfolio from eight to 23 clubs across Alabama, Mississippi and Tennessee. The new locations will operate under Workout Anytime 2.0, a format that pairs standard gym equipment with premium recovery amenities, and Elliott's group plans to open new clubs as well as convert existing gyms. The deal signals that experienced multi-unit franchisees are willing to scale aggressively in the value gym segment when a brand adds recovery offerings, a combination that operators and investors in adjacent categories should watch.
Source: Athletech News →
 
Policy watch
SEPA direct debit failures flagged as a revenue risk in DACH markets
At FitNation München on 25 November 2026, a session addressed how to reduce payment failures, chargebacks and silent cancellations under SEPA direct debit, the dominant membership payment method in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Studio operators in those markets were reminded that managing payment failure proactively is a material revenue protection task, not just an administrative one.
 
Stat
37
live group exercise classes per week at FitX's new Düsseldorf location
A 37-class weekly timetable at a single low-cost site sets a high benchmark for programming density and raises the competitive bar for independent studios in the same catchment area.

01
Triathlon App Stamina Raises $2M Seed Round Backed by Olympic Champion
London-based triathlon training app Stamina raised $2 million in seed funding, with backers including Olympic cycling champion Greg Van Avermaet, Belgian funds Syndicate One and 100IN, content creator Average Rob and former professional basketball player Tomas Van Den Spiegel. Founded by Willem Duyck and Shuowang He, Stamina uses a proprietary training algorithm built with coaches and professional triathletes to deliver personalized swim, bike and run plans, and has surpassed 50,000 downloads since launching in 2025. The raise signals growing investor appetite for endurance coaching tools that sit between expensive one-on-one coaching and generic training plans, a gap coaches and studio operators in the triathlon and endurance space may increasingly face from app-based competitors.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Therabody acquires thermal wearable IP from Embr Labs for women's health
Therabody acquired the intellectual property of Embr Labs, maker of the Wave wrist wearable that delivers precision heating and cooling to address hot flashes and sleep disruption, on 18 November 2026. Embr Labs, an MIT spinout, had sold nearly 250,000 devices before the deal; Therabody plans to fold the thermal technology and research into a women's portfolio that already includes PowerDot, its electrical nerve stimulation device with a period pain mode, building on a women's initiative it launched in 2025. For brands and operators in recovery and wellness, the deal signals that the menopause category is moving from passive monitoring into active, real-time symptom management, a direction also being pursued by Samphire Neuro, OhmBody and Eight Sleep.
Source: Fitt Insider →
03
Seca sales manager makes case for reframing body composition scanners on Club Solutions podcast
Ashley Ziegler Henzler, senior sales manager at seca, appeared on the Club Solutions Magazine podcast hosted by editor Taylor Gabhart to argue that gym operators should position body composition scanners as health analyzers rather than what she called 'fat scanners.' She said clubs serving wearable-literate and GLP-1 members risk losing those members to apps and AI chatbots if operators keep the conversation focused only on weight and body fat. Ziegler Henzler also described a scan day at a Charleston club where sessions with seniors and women asking about menopause surfaced new programme opportunities for the operator.
Source: Club Solutions →
04
McKinsey: U.S. wellness market tops $700B, growing up to 10% a year
McKinsey & Company's fifth Future of Wellness report found the U.S. wellness market exceeds $700 billion and is expanding at 5% to 10% annually. A survey of more than 10,000 consumers across China, Germany, the U.K. and the U.S. found roughly 40% say current offerings fall short in longevity, mental health and mobility, a gap that has persisted since 2024. For studio operators and coaches, that unmet demand points to categories where differentiated programming may find a receptive market.
Source: Athletech News →
05
ACISO Consulting raffles 12 months of consulting and online marketing
ACISO Consulting, a fitness industry consulting firm, is running a prize draw offering one winning club a full year of business development support and online marketing services. The prize follows two first-place wins at the bodyLIFE Award 2026, one in the consulting category and one in online marketing. Only clubs that are not already ACISO clients can enter.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
06
Hone Health raises $228M to expand into peptides and concierge medicine
Longevity platform Hone Health announced a $228M raise on 18 November 2026, combining a $28M equity round led by MarcyPen Capital Partners and $200M in growth financing from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund, adding to $33M raised the previous year. The company, which serves 200,000 patients through diagnostics, AI interpretation, and physician-led programmes, plans to enter peptide and GLP-1 prescribing, metabolic and autoimmune care, and a concierge membership tier that analyses more than 1,600 biomarkers. For fitness operators and coaches, Hone's move into peptides, GLP-1 prescriptions, and advanced diagnostics signals that well-funded digital health platforms are building clinical services that overlap directly with recovery, body composition, and performance programming.
Source: Fitt Insider →
 
Stat
40%
share of consumers surveyed by McKinsey who say current wellness offerings fall short on longevity, mental health and mobility
McKinsey surveyed more than 10,000 consumers across China, Germany, the UK and the US for its fifth Future of Wellness report, and that unmet demand has persisted since 2024, pointing to categories where differentiated programming may find a receptive market.

✓ Read: Review the retention literature on member goal-setting frequency. Research consistently shows that members who revisit a documented goal with a coach at least once a month churn at lower rates, giving you a low-cost argument for scheduling regular check-ins rather than relying on drop-in assessments.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Wednesday, 18 November 2026
item.description: Today's issue covers Orangetheory's GLP-1 coach training programme, an Australian reformer Pilates franchise heading to Miami and Dallas, and iFIT's new voice AI coaching tool.
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Wednesday, 18 November 2026 · Weekday
Orangetheory trains 6,500+ coaches for GLP-1 members, @pilates 24/7 enters US & iFIT launches AI coach
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Today's issue covers Orangetheory's GLP-1 coach training programme, an Australian reformer Pilates franchise heading to Miami and Dallas, and iFIT's new voice AI coaching tool.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
Wellness Monster
closed first seed round on 17 November 2026, led by Grip Ventures with angel participation; amount not disclosed
 
The rundown
01
60-Studio Pilates Franchise @pilates 24/7 Plans US Entry in Miami and Dallas
Australian reformer Pilates franchise @pilates 24/7, which operates 60 studios across Australia and New Zealand and serves around 12,000 members, plans to open its first two US studios in Miami and Dallas in early 2027. Founded in 2021 by Tara and Russell Jarrett, the brand uses a tech-enabled model that gives members round-the-clock access to reformers via individual screens and headphones, with more than 700 on-demand classes on its proprietary platform, rather than relying on scheduled instructor-led sessions. The move signals growing international appetite for unstaffed, on-demand reformer Pilates formats, giving US studio operators a direct read on how that model may compete in the Florida and Texas markets.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Orangetheory trains 6,500+ coaches with NASM to support GLP-1 medication users
Orangetheory Fitness announced a partnership with the National Academy of Sports Medicine (NASM) to train its entire global coaching network of more than 6,500 coaches to support members taking GLP-1 weight-loss medications, calling itself the first fitness brand to do so at that scale. NASM brings more than 35 years of experience educating fitness professionals. With roughly 1 in 8 U.S. adults currently on a GLP-1 medication and more than half of those users saying medication alone is not enough for lasting results, studio operators who build coach expertise around this population may have a competitive advantage in retaining and attracting that growing member segment.
Source: Club Solutions →
03
YTTP opens its fifth Reformer Pilates studio in Berlin
YTTP, the boutique chain founded in Cologne, opened its fifth Reformer Pilates studio in Berlin on 14 and 15 November 2026, located at Backfabrik, Saarbrücker Strasse 36–38 in the Prenzlauer Berg district. The studio covers 300 square metres and holds 35 Reformer machines from the brand Your Reformer, distributed in Germany by Matrix. The opening is one of four studios YTTP plans to launch in the fourth quarter of 2026, a pace that signals growing investor and operator appetite for Reformer Pilates formats in German cities.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
04
iFIT launches Tailor, a voice-based AI coaching tool for members
iFIT has launched Tailor, a voice-based AI coach that holds adaptive conversations with iFIT members, as a central part of the connected fitness company's strategy. For operators and brands watching the connected fitness space, iFIT is signalling that conversational AI coaching is now a core product investment, not a side feature.
Source: Athletech News →
05
Wellness Monster closes seed round led by Grip Ventures
Canadian kids' snack brand Wellness Monster closed its first seed round on November 17, 2026, led by Grip Ventures with participation from angel investors; the amount was not disclosed. The brand, founded by former Mars executive and ex-President of Love Child Organics Brittany Compton, launched in June 2025 and now sells allergen-friendly, nutrient-dense snacks including an 8g-protein Power Bites product across approximately 180 retail stores in Canada, including Whole Foods Market Canada and Metro. For fitness operators stocking or recommending kids' nutrition products, the round signals early retail traction for high-protein, allergen-friendly formats in the children's snack category.
Source: Dealroom →
 
Stat
1 in 8
US adults currently taking a GLP-1 weight-loss medication
With that share of the adult population on GLP-1 drugs, most studios of any size are already coaching members who use them, making staff education on the topic a practical operational need rather than a niche concern.

✓ Track: Monitor your studio's member retention data by programme type each quarter. Members who attend at least twice a week in their first 60 days tend to stay longer, so use that window to identify and follow up with new members who are dropping below that frequency.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Tuesday, 17 November 2026
item.description: Daymond John has taken ownership stakes in four Ultimate Longevity Center franchises as the longevity brand prepares to open its first locations in January 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday, 17 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Tuesday, 17 November 2026 · Weekday
Daymond John buys into 4 Ultimate Longevity Center franchises, FitX drops 12-month contract & HFA retention podcast
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Daymond John has taken ownership stakes in four Ultimate Longevity Center franchises as the longevity brand prepares to open its first locations in January 2027.
Sqwod
 
The rundown
01
Daymond John buys into 4 Ultimate Longevity Center franchises
Daymond John, founder of apparel brand Fubu and investor on the television show 'Shark Tank,' has taken ownership stakes in four Ultimate Longevity Center locations. The longevity franchise, co-founded by Gary Brecka and Anthony Geisler and part of Geisler's Sequel Brands portfolio, has sold more than 350 franchise territories globally since launching franchise sales earlier in 2026, including 200 in its first four months. Its first locations are set to open in January 2027 in Arizona, Colorado, Florida and Southern California, with 50 Australia locations also planned, signalling strong investor and franchisee demand in the longevity category.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Hapana sales director joins HFA podcast on retention at scale
Jody Hinman, North America Director of Sales at Hapana, spoke with Pam Kufahl, VP of Marketing and Communications at the Health and Fitness Association, in a podcast published by the association. They discussed where retention problems emerge as fitness businesses grow from one location to many, what operators do differently in a member's first 30 days, and how location-level data can flag members who are likely to cancel. Operators running multiple sites may find the conversation useful given its focus on maintaining a consistent member experience and keeping strong staff as a business scales.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
03
FitX drops 12-month minimum contract, new memberships now monthly cancellable
German gym chain FitX ended its 12-month minimum membership term on 16 November 2026, replacing it with contracts that are cancellable on a monthly basis. The monthly fee stays at 29 euros and the one-time registration fee stays at 29 euros, with access to more than 110 studios across Germany and all included amenities unchanged. The move signals that a large low-cost operator is treating contract flexibility as a tool to lower the barrier for new members, a competitive pressure other gym operators will need to weigh.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
04
Yahoo Finance publishes seasonal returns chart for WELUF
Yahoo Finance has published a seasonal returns chart for Integrated Wellness Acquisition Corp, ticker WELUF.
Source: Yahoo Finance UK →

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Monday, 16 November 2026
item.description: Crunch Fitness is pursuing an $800 million bond sale backed by franchise revenue, while a Hamburg ad network gives German studios access to brand budgets.
item.content:encoded:
Monday, 16 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Monday, 16 November 2026 · Weekday
Crunch Fitness seeks $800M franchise bond sale, Fitvertise networks 2,200+ German gyms for ad revenue & Pete Bates on language and self-acceptance
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Crunch Fitness is pursuing an $800 million bond sale backed by franchise revenue, while a Hamburg ad network gives German studios access to brand budgets.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
Crunch Fitness
 $800 million
franchise-revenue-backed bond sale led by Guggenheim Securities, not yet finalised
 
Connect the dots
Crunch Fitness targets $800M through franchise-backed bond sale
Crunch Fitness is seeking to raise about $800 million through a whole-business securitisation, a structure in which bonds are backed by predictable franchise revenue streams rather than physical assets. Guggenheim Securities is leading the deal. The planned structure includes $650 million of bonds with an average life of around five years sold to institutional investors, a $100 million privately placed note drawable at a later date, and a $50 million variable funding facility. Early investor talks have begun, though terms are not finalised and may change.
For studio operators and franchise investors, the deal signals that franchise-fee revenue is being treated as a bankable, bond-grade asset. That matters because it reflects how lenders assess the durability of the low-cost, high-volume gym model at scale.
 
The rundown
01
Pete Bates writes on violence, language and self-acceptance for Global Wellness Institute
Pete Bates, founder of The Pete Bates Project, published a guest essay on the Global Wellness Institute's platform reflecting on how an inability to articulate thoughts and feelings drove him toward physical confrontation as a young man. He describes the behaviour not as strength but as a failure in learned responses to being challenged, and states it does not excuse any act of violence.
Source: Global Wellness Institute →
02
Crunch Fitness seeks $800 million in franchise-backed bond sale
Crunch Fitness is looking to raise about $800 million through a bond sale backed by its franchise revenue, with Guggenheim Securities leading the deal. The structure would include $650 million of bonds with an average life of about five years sold to institutional investors, a $100 million privately placed note drawable at a later date, and a $50 million variable funding facility. Early talks with investors have begun, though plans and details have not been finalized and may still change.
Source: Athletech News →
03
BuDhaGirl CEO challenges wellness leaders to prioritise intention over metrics
Jessica Jesse, co-chair of GWS 2026 and founder, CEO and creative director of BuDhaGirl, challenged wellness leaders to look beyond technology, longevity and performance metrics, arguing that intention, meaning and everyday rituals must also shape the industry's future. Jesse made the remarks in her role as GWS 2026 co-chair.
Source: Health Club Management →
04
Fitvertise aggregates ad inventory across 2,200-plus gyms in Germany
Fitvertise, a Hamburg-based company, has built an advertising network spanning more than 2,200 fitness studios in Germany, including LifeFit Group, EASYFITNESS, and independent owner-operated studios. Brands can book analogue and digital formats across the entire network through a single contact, while studios join at no cost and receive a share of the resulting ad revenue. For independent studio operators too small to appear in a national media plan on their own, the network offers a way to access brand advertising budgets that have historically bypassed gyms: German government figures show companies spent around 2.7 billion euros on sports sponsorship in 2019.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
 
Stat
2.7 billion euros
annual German corporate spending on sports sponsorship in 2019, per German government figures
German gyms have historically received little of that budget, but Fitvertise's network of more than 2,200 studios now gives brands a single point of access to book analogue and digital formats across independent and chain locations nationwide.

item.description: YouFit Gyms lands private equity backing for a strength and recovery overhaul, while Bodi enters the Hyrox training space and supplement strips attract early capital.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday, 15 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Sunday, 15 November 2026 · Weekday
YouFit secures $10M+ for club refreshes, Bodi targets Hyrox market & dissolvable strips raise $1M
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
YouFit Gyms lands private equity backing for a strength and recovery overhaul, while Bodi enters the Hyrox training space and supplement strips attract early capital.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
YouFit Gyms
 $10M+
private equity investment from Skyline Investors to refresh clubs and support growth
▲  Raise
Sleep or Die
 $1M
raised from True Beauty Ventures for dissolvable bedtime supplement strips
 
Connect the dots
YouFit's $10M+ refresh puts strength and recovery at the centre
YouFit Gyms announced a $10 million-plus investment from Skyline Investors, a Los Angeles-based private equity firm, to refresh existing clubs and support growth. The first phase covers 12 clubs in Florida, with updates to strength floors, recovery amenities and functional training space. The deal marks Skyline Investors' first move into the fitness and wellness sector.
For studio and gym operators, the investment is a signal that private equity sees member demand for strength training and recovery as a fundable thesis. If you have not yet audited your own floor layout and amenity mix against what members are asking for in those two areas, this week is a reasonable moment to start.
 
The rundown
01
Bodi launches Insanity: Unhinged, a 100-day hybrid training program
Bodi, formerly known as Beachbody, launched Insanity: Unhinged, a 100-day home training program designed for Hyrox and hybrid fitness events. The program is led by three-time Hyrox world champion Hunter McIntyre and executive produced by Shaun T, creator of the original Insanity; participants train seven days a week across 45 workouts in three progressive phases, with weekday sessions of 30 to 45 minutes and a Saturday competition day. The move signals that home fitness platforms are positioning directly against the Hyrox training market, which gyms and studios have been chasing.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Fitness operators report ongoing growth as competition and acquisition costs rise
Australasian Leisure Management Magazine reported that fitness operators are experiencing ongoing growth while competition and acquisition costs are also rising. No further figures, dates, or parties were named in the source. Operators and investors considering acquisitions should note that rising acquisition costs are a current market condition in this sector.
Source: Australasian Leisure Management Magazine →
03
YouFit Gyms secures $10M-plus from Skyline Investors for club refreshes
YouFit Gyms announced a $10 million-plus investment from Skyline Investors, a Los Angeles-based private equity firm, to refresh existing clubs and support growth. The first phase covers 12 clubs in Florida, with updates to strength floors, recovery amenities and functional training space. The deal signals that value-segment gym operators are attracting private equity capital specifically to meet rising member demand for strength training and recovery offerings.
Source: Club Solutions →
04
Dissolvable supplement strips draw $1M raise and 4K waitlist amid $79B category shift
Oral supplement strips are gaining commercial ground in the $79B supplement market, with Sleep or Die raising $1M from True Beauty Ventures and building a 4,000-person waitlist for its bedtime strips, while NuStrips secured shelf space at Erewhon and Urban Outfitters. Other entrants include Pemi, targeting perimenopause support, Wizard Wellness for allergy care, Smart Strips for cognitive function using alpha-GPC, Nuet for gut health, and Riize with 50mg of NAD+ per strip. Fitt Insider noted that better bioavailability for strips is not yet proven, meaning studio and brand operators evaluating this format should weigh efficacy evidence before committing to partnerships or retail placement.
Source: Fitt Insider →
05
LEVL Strength launches isokinetic home training system with 500 lb magnetic resistance
LEVL Strength has introduced a portable, adjustable home strength machine that delivers up to 500 pounds of magnetic resistance with no installation or fixed weights required. Its isokinetic mode, called Iso-K Mode, adjusts resistance in real time to match the user's force output across the full range of motion, and the company claims an effective workout is achievable in as few as five reps per exercise. For coaches and operators, the device signals growing commercial interest in adaptive resistance technology that removes the need for a traditional weight room setup.
Source: Wellworthy →
 
Stat
$79B
size of the global supplement category
The scale of the supplement market explains why new delivery formats such as dissolvable strips are attracting early investment, even before efficacy claims have been independently verified.

Friday, 13 November 2026 View online →
DAILY
Friday, 13 November 2026 · Weekday
Men now a third of Pilates participants, HFA names permanent CEO & PIRL launches studio brand-deal platform
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Men now make up roughly a third of Pilates participants, reshaping studio demand, while the HFA named a permanent CEO and a new platform launched to connect studios with brand partners.
Sqwod
 
5 jobs this week

See all jobs →
 
Connect the dots
Men are now a third of Pilates participants: what it means for studios
Men now account for roughly one third of Pilates participants, a marked shift in a category that was once dominated by women. Studios including Club Pilates, STRONG Pilates, and solidcore are responding by aligning their programming and messaging to reach both men and women. Industry observers describe this as a structural change in who is walking through the door, not a short-term spike.
For studio operators, a broader co-ed audience affects class design, marketing language, and potentially pricing and scheduling decisions. Studios that have not yet reviewed their messaging and programming mix for gender inclusivity have a concrete reason to do so now.
 
The rundown
01
Men now make up a third of Pilates participants, reshaping studio demand
Men account for roughly one third of Pilates participants, a marked shift in a category that was once dominated by women. Studios including Club Pilates, STRONG Pilates, and solidcore are responding to growing co-ed demand by aligning programming and messaging to reach both men and women. For studio operators, the broader audience represents a structural change in who is walking through the door, not a short-term spike.
Source: Fitt Insider →
02
WHOOP launches in-app social network for health and activity data
WHOOP launched WHOOP Humans, an in-app social network allowing its 3 million members to add friends, share Sleep, Recovery, and Strain scores, upload activities with photos, and comment on posts. The company says 57 percent of its members already belong to at least one Team, and members open the app eight times per day. For fitness platforms and brands, the move signals that keeping social activity inside a wearable ecosystem, rather than ceding it to Strava and its 200 million-plus users, is becoming a direct competitive priority.
Source: Fitt Insider →
03
HFA Names Greta Wagner Permanent President and CEO, Unveils Three-Year Plan
The Health & Fitness Association named Greta Wagner its permanent president and CEO on November 12 at Beyond Activ Americas in Dallas, after she spent six months in an interim role. Wagner led development of a three-year strategic plan, created with the HFA Board of Directors and industry stakeholders, aimed at delivering greater member value, strengthening advocacy, and expanding the industry's influence. For studio and gym operators who rely on HFA for lobbying and resources, the plan signals a more focused effort to make the association a stronger advocate for the industry.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
04
Former Barry's and Grüns Execs Launch Studio Brand-Deal Platform PIRL
Ali Kaltman, formerly head of partnerships at Grüns, and Daniel Rabinovich, formerly VP of brand partnerships at Barry's, co-founded and launched PIRL on November 9, 2026. The platform matches brands with studios based on fitness discipline, member demographics, and geographic market, handles contracting and payments, and already counts Pvolve, SoulCycle, and Strong Pilates among its studio partners. Studios list for free; PIRL charges a fee on the brand side and holds funds until class attendance is verified before releasing payouts, giving studio operators a no-cost way to access brand revenue with a built-in attendance check.
Source: Athletech News →
05
Gantner launches face-recognition access system GT7 powered by XS4 Face
Gantner, an access control technology company, has released the GT7 powered by XS4 Face, a facial recognition system designed for fitness studios and health practices. The system identifies members with a brief look at a camera, requiring no card, smartphone or wristband, and is built to meet data protection and security standards. For studio operators, the technology can reduce front-desk workload, ease peak-hour congestion and support unstaffed or low-staff 24-hour access models.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
 
Policy watch
HFA names Greta Wagner permanent president and CEO, launches three-year plan
The Health and Fitness Association named Greta Wagner its permanent president and chief executive on November 12, 2026, after six months in an interim role. Wagner led development of a three-year strategic plan, created with the HFA board and industry stakeholders, focused on member value, advocacy, and expanding the industry's influence.
 
Stat
57%
Share of WHOOP's 3 million members who already belong to at least one in-app Team
The figure shows that social and competitive features inside wearable apps already have strong adoption, which matters for fitness platforms and studio operators deciding whether to integrate with or compete against wearable ecosystems.
